boards.title: Your First Weekend at Trinity College, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A gentle, campus-centered first-weekend loop: get oriented outdoors, find useful indoor anchors, then check the arts and event calendars for a plan.

cards.title: Start at Gates Quadrangle
cards.subtitle: Stop 1 · Campus outdoor orientation point
cards.notes: Use the pedestrian paths and open lawn as a first landmark, then orient yourself to nearby Mather Hall before heading farther across campus.
cards.short_summary: A named open campus space directly in front of Mather Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: Trinity identifies Gates Quadrangle as the campus area immediately in front of Mather Hall, reshaped into an open pedestrian space.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus space; follow posted campus access guidance.

cards.title: Make a Mather Hall meal plan
cards.subtitle: Stop 2 · Mather Hall
cards.notes: Check the dining information and your meal access, then use the hall as a practical reset point before continuing the campus walk.
cards.short_summary: Trinity's central dining area, renovated with expanded seating and multiple food stations.
cards.evidence_claim: Trinity describes Mather Dining Hall as its central dining area and reports that its renovation added seating, food stations, and study-capable booths.
cards.source_title: Mather Dining Hall Renovation Reenvisions the Student Experience
cards.access_notes: Dining access and offerings depend on current College and dining-service arrangements.

cards.title: Walk the Long Walk in daylight
cards.subtitle: Stop 3 · Historic campus core
cards.notes: Take the full outdoor route at an easy pace and notice the arches, towers, and quadrangle views; stay on normal public pedestrian paths.
cards.short_summary: A 925-foot historic campus route made up of Seabury Hall, Jarvis Hall, and Northam Towers.
cards.evidence_claim: Trinity documents the 925-foot Long Walk as comprising Seabury Hall, Jarvis Hall, and Northam Towers on the Summit Street campus.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor route; use normal paths and respect residential and building access rules.

cards.title: Pause on the Main Quad
cards.subtitle: Stop 4 · Between the Long Walk and campus landmarks
cards.notes: Use this central lawn to get your bearings, locate the Long Walk and Chapel, and check the College calendar for an appropriate public event.
cards.short_summary: The central quad used for Trinity's Convocation and Matriculation ceremony.
cards.evidence_claim: Trinity's 2025 Convocation and Matriculation ceremony gathered new students and the Trinity community on the Main Quad.
cards.source_title: Convocation Welcomes New Students to Trinity, Marks Start of Academic Year
cards.access_notes: Outdoor space; event setups and access can change.

cards.entity_name: Statue of Bishop Thomas Church Brownell
cards.title: Find the Bishop Brownell statue
cards.subtitle: Stop 5 · Main Quad landmark
cards.notes: Look for the bronze monument on the Main Quad and use it as a clear meeting landmark while learning a little about the College's founding.
cards.short_summary: A nearly 30-foot monument to Trinity's founder and first president.
cards.evidence_claim: Trinity states that the Bishop Thomas Church Brownell statue has stood in the center of the Main Quad since 1878 and commemorates the College's founder.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor landmark on the Main Quad.

cards.entity_name: Raether Library and Information Technology Center
cards.title: Locate Raether's reading rooms
cards.subtitle: Stop 6 · Raether Library and Information Technology Center
cards.notes: Find the library entrance and identify a reading-room destination for a later study session; verify current building access and service details on arrival.
cards.short_summary: A campus library center with documented reading-room space.
cards.evidence_claim: Trinity's photography locations page identifies the Engelhard Reading Room in the Raether Center.
cards.source_title: Filming and Photography at Trinity College
cards.access_notes: Confirm current library access and service hours with Trinity Libraries.

cards.title: Step into Watkinson Library
cards.subtitle: Stop 7 · Inside Raether Library
cards.notes: Note the special-collections library for a future visit, then ask staff about current procedures before planning research with rare or archival materials.
cards.short_summary: Trinity's special-collections library and repository for College Archives.
cards.evidence_claim: Trinity says the Watkinson Library is on the main level of Raether Library and Information Technology Center and serves as the repository of Trinity College Archives.
cards.source_title: The Watkinson Library: Bringing Rare Books and Special Collections to Life
cards.access_notes: The library serves students, faculty, and the public; confirm current reading-room procedures before visiting.

cards.title: Check the Austin Arts Center calendar
cards.subtitle: Stop 8 · Arts venues and gallery
cards.notes: Review the current listings for a performance, exhibition, or concert, and reserve ahead when an event page says a reservation is required.
cards.short_summary: Trinity's arts hub, housing theater, music, studio-art venues, and Widener Gallery.
cards.evidence_claim: Trinity identifies Austin Arts Center as its cultural hub and says its sponsored events are currently free, though many require reservations.
cards.access_notes: AAC says many events require reservations; check the specific event listing before going.

cards.title: Look for a Chapel Music event
cards.subtitle: Stop 9 · Trinity College Chapel
cards.notes: Check the Chapel Music schedule for a concert or service that fits your weekend, then follow the event's accessibility and arrival guidance.
cards.short_summary: A campus chapel and gathering place that hosts services, concerts, and the Organ Festival.
cards.evidence_claim: Trinity says the Chapel hosts weekly services, concerts, the Albert Schweitzer Organ Festival, Matriculation, and Baccalaureate; Chapel Music events are free unless noted.
cards.access_notes: All Chapel Music events are free and open to the public unless otherwise noted; no tickets are required.

cards.title: End with a Cinestudio screening
cards.subtitle: Stop 10 · Summit Street and College Terrace
cards.notes: Use the official schedule to select a screening, confirm its start time and ticket details, and arrive through normal theater access points.
cards.short_summary: A nonprofit, single-screen independent theater located on Trinity's campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Cinestudio identifies itself as a nonprofit independent theater on Trinity's campus at Summit Street and College Terrace and publishes current showtimes online.
cards.access_notes: Check the official showtime page for the specific film and ticket availability.
